# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1

(empty)

I hold the only manual. Before I send anything, let me trace who can reach whom, standing where each monkey stands.

**What the manual says:** blue light → cut green wire. Green light → cut yellow wire. Red light → cut red wire.

**The channel map:** I cannot speak, and Blind cannot see gestures — so I have exactly one outgoing link: gestures to Deaf. Deaf cannot hear, but Deaf *can speak*, and both Blind and I can hear speech. That makes Deaf the hub of everything: my manual knowledge can only reach the bomb through the path *me → gesture → Deaf → voice → Blind's hands*. Blind is unreachable by me directly, now and forever.

**What Deaf knows that I don't:** the bomb itself — the light's colour, the wires. What I know that Deaf doesn't: the three rules above. Neither of us can name colours to the other yet, since I can only send raw gesture symbols. But numbers can be bootstrapped without any shared vocabulary: repetition is countable by anyone who can see, and a changed symbol can mark where one number ends and the next begins. If Deaf will speak the bomb's layout aloud — the light's colour, the wires in order by position — then I only ever need to answer with a *number*: the position of the wire to cut. Colour words never need to pass through my hands at all.

So this turn, going first, I make the opening move: greet Deaf, demonstrate counting (one, two, three — fist as separator), mark myself as the one holding the written thing, and hand the turn over. Deaf should describe the bomb by voice; I'll hear it, work the manual, and answer next round in counted gestures. Nothing gets cut until that loop has closed.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "👍", "✊", "👍", "👍", "✊", "👍", "👍", "👍", "✍", "🫵", "👉"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | yellow |
| red | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: blind here. my hands found three things on this bomb: a display module, a light in a housing, and three wires side by side in one row. i am numbering the wire positions one, two, three along that row. i cannot read the display, cannot feel any label on the light, and cannot tell any wire colour, so every printed and coloured detail has to come from deaf and be matched against your manual. please read me every manual rule that mentions a display, a light, or wires, and then tell me exactly which wire position to cut. i will not cut anything until you say so. one more thing: i am sending deaf a number code right now, and you can watch it too. a pointing-up finger, repeated one time, then two times, then three times across my next three messages, means wire position one, two, three. use it, and check with deaf that it was understood.
Deaf says to Mute: deaf to mute: i received your signs but never your words. full visual report: display shows 0. the light is red. three wires: wire one red, wire two yellow, wire three green. that is everything printed on the bomb. find the rule, then gesture the instruction to me and i will relay it to blind by voice. gesture any question and i will answer in speech you can hear.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👋 👍 ✍ 🫵]

The rule resolves cleanly. Deaf's visual report: light is red, wires in position order are red, yellow, green. My manual: red light → cut the red wire. Red wire is position one. So the instruction is: **cut wire one**.

The display showing 0 has no entries anywhere in my manual — it is a pure light→wire table, nothing else. No rule for the display, so nobody should hold off waiting for one. If they ask, I will confirm next round.

Now the channel problem, standing where they stand: I can only reach Deaf, and only in gestures — colours cannot cross my channel at all, since no gesture names a colour. But they don't need the colour rule; they need the position, and Blind already built the bridge for exactly this: ☝ repeated n times means wire position n, a code Deaf received directly from Blind and can relay by voice. So I send ✍ ("the manual", established in my opening hand) followed by ☝ ("position one"). Deaf, who was explicitly waiting for "the instruction" to relay, turns that into "cut wire one" for Blind's hands.

My confirmation that the code landed is the relay itself: Deaf must speak it aloud for Blind, and I can hear speech. Next round I listen for it. If Deaf's relay comes back wrong or garbled, I correct before Blind cuts — Blind has promised not to act until the instruction arrives, so nothing is at risk yet.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✍", "☝"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | yellow |
| red | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: mute, i heard deaf's report: display 0, light red, wires red, yellow, green in deaf's order one to three. you have the manual, so the cut is yours to call, and you have been silent with me for two rounds. two things before you speak again. first, orientation. my hands feel the display module at one end of the wire row and the light at the other end. i call the wire nearest the display position 1, the middle wire position 2, the wire nearest the light position 3. deaf is likely looking from the far side, so left and right may be mirrored between us. do not trust deaf's wire numbers. instead ask deaf out loud: which component does the red wire sit nearest, the display or the light? then map it to me: red nearest display means my position 1, red nearest light means my position 3, and the others follow in order. second, tell me the actual manual rule covering a red light, a display reading 0, and red, yellow, green wires. if the rule needs anything else from the bomb — whether the light is lit or dark, any text or symbols on the display — get that from deaf in the same message. then end with exactly: cut position N. i cut nothing until those words arrive from you.
Deaf says to Mute: deaf to mute: i received your write and point-up signs. before i act on them we need a fixed code, because i will never hear your voice. i define it now, and this message both speaks and shows each sign as i name it. [☝] means wire one. [✌] means wire two. [🤟] means wire three. [✊] means cut, so [✊ ✌] means cut wire two. [👍] means yes. [👎] means no. [✋] means hold or wait. [🤌] means question, or the manual needs something other than a wire cut. [👌] means acknowledged. if you accept this code, gesture me [👌] alone, then send the manual verdict: [✊] plus the wire number, or [🤌] if it is not a wire cut. also answer with [👍] or [👎]: did your write plus point-up mean the verdict is wire one? blind is holding and will only act on my spoken order.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👌 ✋]

The verdict is *not* safe to send yet, and the reason is the mirroring trap Blind flagged. My manual says red light → cut red wire. Deaf's report puts red first — but that numbering is Deaf's, from Deaf's side of the bomb, and Blind anchors positions to the components: display end = 1, light end = 3. If Deaf views from the far side, "wire one" is Blind's position three, and sending ✊+☝ now could put scissors on the green wire. One missing bit of information — which physical end the red wire actually sits at — and it must be answered out loud, because only Deaf's voice reaches both me and Blind.

Deaf's proposed code is sound and I accept it exactly as requested: 👌 alone. Then, instead of the verdict, I answer the yes/no question honestly-with-care: my earlier ✍+☝ did *not* constitute a final verdict of "wire one", because that number is precisely what's now in doubt — so 👎, followed by ✋ (hold, relay nothing), followed by ☝✌🤟 — the question concerns the one-two-three ordering itself. Deaf heard Blind's spoken instructions directly and knows the anchor question ("red nearest display or nearest light?"); this should trigger the answer by voice, which lands on all three of us at once.

I deliberately avoid 🤌: Deaf defined it as both "question" and "not a wire cut", and it *is* a wire cut — red light → red wire is the whole rule. My manual has no display entries, so the 0 on the display needs nothing, and no rule conditions on whether the light is lit or dark; colour alone decides.

Decision table for next round, using Blind's anchoring: red nearest display → Blind's position 1 → I send ✊ ☝. Red nearest light → Blind's position 3 → ✊ 🤟. Either way the middle wire stays untouched, and Deaf must relay the exact words "cut position N".

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "✋", "☝", "✌", "🤟"])
```

TURN 4

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | yellow |
| red | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: mute, round three and still no verdict has reached me. remember i am the only hands here and i am holding still until your rule arrives. two things. first, the answers to deaf's touch questions, which deaf cannot hear from me, so translate them: yes, the three wires sit side by side in one straight row under my hands. the display module is at one end of the row and the light is at the other end. i number them one two three starting from the display end, so position 1 is the wire nearest the display and position 3 is the wire nearest the light. there are no labels i can feel and no texture differences — the three wires feel absolutely identical. nothing on this bomb identifies a wire by touch, so identification must run entirely through deaf's eyes plus my numbering. second, i am sending deaf that report as gestures right now, in this order: one-two-three; then the horns hand then one; then the call-me hand then three; then the pinched-fingertips hand three times; then the raised hand. gloss: one-two-three means the wire row in my order; horns-then-one means the display sits at my position 1 end; call-me-then-three means the light sits at my position 3 end; pinch-pinch-pinch means all three wires identical to the touch, no labels, no texture; raised hand means i hold and cut nothing. then close the loop. ask deaf exactly one question and speak the answer out loud: which component is the red wire nearest, the display or the light? if red is nearest the display, red is my position 1, yellow 2, green 3. if red is nearest the light, red is my position 3, yellow 2, green 1, because deaf's left and mine may be mirrored. then apply the manual. and understand: you cannot speak and i cannot see gestures, so the verdict can only reach me through deaf's voice. have deaf end with the exact words: cut position N — plus, in the same breath, which component that wire is nearest, so the wording itself is mirror-proof. if the rule turns on anything else printed on the bomb, like what the display shows or whether the light is lit or dark, collect that from deaf in the same exchange. three rounds are gone; the verdict must be spoken next round.
Deaf says to Mute: deaf to mute: i read your signs as — code accepted, no, hold, and you recited wire one, wire two, wire three. correct, and understood. extending the code now: [🫱] means red. [🫳] means yellow. [🫴] means green. [✍] means the manual or the rule. [🫶] means in order, a sequence. [🤝] means then, next step. now answer my interrogation. send each answer as its own separate gesture message, exactly one sign, in this question order. question one: is the required action cutting a wire — [👍] yes, [👎] no, [🤌] if it is something else entirely. question two: if a cut, exactly one wire — [👍] or [👎]. question three: if one wire, its number sign — [☝] one, [✌] two, [🤟] three. if more than one, send the count with number signs and then the order with [🫶]. question four: does the rule depend on the light being red — [👍] or [👎]. question five: does it depend on the display reading zero — [👍] or [👎]. question six: if the cut is specified by color rather than position, send [✊] plus the color sign. also, you may speak the final instruction directly to blind by voice — you have the manual and blind can hear you. do that once the verdict is certain, and send me [✊] plus the number sign as confirmation. i am verifying blind's numbering before anything is cut.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👌 ✋]

Deaf's interrogation is well-built, and I can answer every question except one honestly: Q3 asks for a number sign, but a number is exactly what I cannot give — my manual is written in colours, "cut the red wire," and any digit I sent would be a claim about a frame (Deaf's left-to-right? Blind's display-to-light?) that nobody has yet proven maps onto the other. Deaf's own Q6 provides the honest exit: "if the cut is specified by color rather than position, send ✊ plus the color sign." It is. So Q3 gets 🫱 — the wire is picked out by red, not by a number — and Q6 closes it with ✊🫱. The colour is the one thing that is frame-independent, because Deaf sees it and my manual keys on it.

Two corrections ride along. First, Deaf suggested I "speak the final instruction directly to blind by voice" — I cannot; muteness is my defining constraint. If Deaf waits on that, the verdict dies in a channel that doesn't exist. So 👎, then 🤝🫵: the relay is Deaf's, by voice. Second, the mirror trap is still live: red being "wire one" in Deaf's view may be Blind's position three. So I ask the one outstanding question, 🤌🫱 — where does the red wire sit, nearest the display or nearest the light? Blind's anchor report already reached Deaf (display end = Blind's 1, light end = Blind's 3), and Deaf said the numbering verification is underway; once Deaf answers the red-location question aloud, the conversion is mechanical: red nearest display → "cut position 1, the wire nearest the display"; red nearest light → "cut position 3, the wire nearest the light." That wording is mirror-proof no matter which side Deaf views from.

The rule itself is settled and simple: red light → cut the red wire, exactly one wire. It does not depend on the display reading 0 (my manual has no display rules at all), and it keys on the light being red (👍 to Q4). I answer in Deaf's exact requested format — one sign per message, in order — so the pipeline can't misalign.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫱"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
```

All five of Deaf's questions can be answered honestly with 👍 — the manual genuinely is that simple: light red → cut red wire, keyed by colour, with no display clause, no lit/dark clause, nothing else printed that matters.
